forward_vector: I am the manifest of Kokoro's rich face: what was made for each section, and the fingerprint of the words each piece was made against, so the page can say when a piece may lag the text. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.
note: A light face, from the second light round (2026-11-17): one small thing beside one sentence. Made as if it were the only page: one maker who read the page whole, one challenger who was given nothing of the maker's reasoning, one remake, and a second verdict by the same challenger. Made in Enrichment/light-round-2026-11-2/pieces/Kokoro/, where the script, the job and its provenance stay; placed here by the Concierge, with what made it copied from that provenance and not guessed. Loudon approved the line it was made from ("Yes, make them", 2026-11-17, relayed by the working session) and has not seen or heard the finished piece. The section is a proposal until he approves it.

verdicts.file: Kokoro — rich — two commas, a quiet before K.m4a
verdicts.why: Remake, small: words and picture; the sound and the measurements stand. Every tally reproduced. But "0 of 40 … 40 of 40" read like forty independent trials when it is four voices of one sentence, with one voice on the threshold; the picture called the quiet a pause; and its largest box was the quiet after K in the take without commas, the opposite of the page's sentence beside it, unremarked. The challenger's own probe suggested the quiet before K is largely the K's own stop, and it made the May takes exact by re-rendering them.

remade.file: Kokoro — rich — two commas, a quiet before K.m4a
remade.what: The sound did not change. The maker tested both of the challenger's findings before remaking: the May takes confirmed and became the second route; the closure reading did not hold in this sentence (ten letters, two sentences, four voices: commas gave a quiet before the letter in 27 of 40 cases against 9). The picture now says "quiet", marks the long box as "in both reads", and states the evidence as four voices of one sentence with one at the line; the caption claims only K in this sentence. After the second verdict two small fixes were applied by the maker and seen by the working session.
remade.by: the Kokoro maker, the same maker
remade.second_verdict: keep: The picture reads clearly and its figures match the challenger's own decode of the unchanged m4a; scratch rerun byte-identical. On the closure probe the challenger was wrong in part and says so: a stop like K mostly does not get the quiet and vowel-initial letters mostly do. Only an ear can judge whether 110 ms before K is heard as a pause or a crisper K, and whether the bare K sounds run into anything. Nobody has heard it.

pieces.title: Two commas, a quiet before K · drawn
pieces.caption:
**Punctuation changes how this voice phrases a sentence; here is what two commas did to one.** Kokoro reads "The coupling constant K is phrasing density and rhythmic clarity." first without commas, then as the page writes it, "…constant, K, is…".

- **What changed:** with commas, a quiet stretch came before K. In four voices it was there with commas in all four and without commas in none. One voice sits at the line (50 to 60 ms here; 45 ms by the challenger's detector).
- **What did not:** both reads already had a quiet after K.
- **The takes reviewed in May show the same:** re-rendered so Kokoro's own word timings lie on them, the take without commas had no quiet before K, and the take with commas had 210 ms there.

This holds for K in this sentence. With other letters and in another sentence, where the commas' quiet fell varied.

That the bare K has no quiet before it, and does have one after it, is the maker's measurement; the page says it "runs into the next word". Nobody has heard it yet.
